title: Hibernation posture on the hub shape: elicited hibernate-after-idle window and idempotent wake handler (elicited)
context: The hub shape hibernates when idle; the wake handler runs from cold on the next message. The hibernate-after-idle window trades a cold-start hit on the first wake against the memory footprint of an always-warm object. The window is a per-project answer; the shipped default (Cloudflare's platform-default) is fine for most projects but a coordinated-multiplayer workload with tight latency budgets picks a longer window.
decision: The applied blueprint elicits do-hub-hibernate-after-idle-ms at apply time (a bounded millis integer). The wake handler MUST be idempotent-by-contract: repeated wakes on the same last-persisted message do not double-emit downstream state. The shipped HubObject class realises the idempotent-wake contract via a boolean _woke gate paired with the persisted lastBroadcast key; the anatomy assertion covers the once-per-wake doWakeUp event under AC-33110-1.
consequences: Projects with tight latency budgets pick a longer window; projects with tight memory budgets pick a shorter one. Standards trace clause: generic enterprise practice (the hibernate-after-idle trade is a general enterprise-tier state-hosting choice, not a Cloudflare-specific claim; Cloudflare's platform-default is the shipped fallback).
